findings.key_quote: Cost of subscription revenue increased during the three and nine months ended August 28, 2026 as compared to the three and nine months ended August 29, 2025 primarily due to the following: Components of % Change 2026-2025 QTD ... Hosting services and data center costs 22 %
findings.justification: This evidence directly addresses Q3 FY2026 (the three months ended August 28, 2026). It states that cost of subscription revenue increased 'primarily due to' hosting services and data center costs contributing 22% of the total 24% change. Since 22% out of 24% represents the overwhelming majority (over 90%) of the increase, this establishes that hosting and data center costs were the main reason for the rise in cost of subscription revenue in Q3 FY2026.

This evidence shows that cost of subscription revenue for the three months ended August 28, 2026 (Q3 FY2026) was $633 million compared to $510 million in the prior year, representing a 24% increase. This confirms that cost of subscription revenue did rise in Q3 FY2026, which is a necessary component of the claim.

findings.key_quote: Cost of subscription revenue increased during the three and six months ended May 29, 2026 as compared to the three and six months ended May 30, 2025 primarily due to the following: Components of % Change 2026-2025 QTD ... Hosting services and data center costs 16 %
findings.justification: This evidence is for Q2 FY2026 (three months ended May 29, 2026), not Q3 FY2026. While it shows a similar pattern of hosting and data center costs being the primary driver (16% out of 16% total change), it addresses a different period than the claim's Q3 FY2026 period.
